gained.note: Percent increase: v times (100 + p) / 100, worked out in decimals with no rounding of its own. Confirmed.

rated.note: p percent of v, in decimals with no rounding of its own. Confirmed.

reduced.note: Percent decrease: v times (100 - p) / 100, in decimals with no rounding of its own. Confirmed.

to_int.note: Conversion to a whole number: rounds half up (2.5 becomes 3). Confirmed. It is not truncation.

state_value.name: Value one state adds to a running total
state_value.explain: A state adds nothing unless the character has it. Then it adds either a flat number or a percent of another stat.

state_value_counts.name: Value one state adds to a running total (own-stat, count and sum modes)
state_value_counts.explain: Same idea as state_value, but the amount depends on the character's own stat, on how many buffs or ailments it has, or on their total.

dot_scaling.name: Scaling of damage-over-time, reflect, pursuit and delayed damage
dot_scaling.explain: The damage is raised by the attacker's matching scaling percent.

cross_element_boost.name: Burn / Frostbite / Electric cross-boost
cross_element_boost.explain: The other elements' scaling counts at a reduced strength, applied one after another.

direct_damage_vs_ailment.name: Direct damage against a target with ailments
direct_damage_vs_ailment.explain: For each ailment the target has, direct damage is raised by the attacker's bonus against that ailment, one after another.

stat_bonus_chain.name: How a stat's bonuses combine
stat_bonus_chain.expr: clamp(reduced(gained(to_int(max(0, raw + at_total + plus - minus + extra_flat)), to_int(star) + extra_pct), to_int(div)), 0, 9999999)
stat_bonus_chain.explain: A stat starts from its base value plus flat bonuses minus flat penalties (never below 0), rounded half up. All percent bonuses are added together and applied once. Percent reductions are applied last. The result is capped.

crit_damage.name: Critical hit damage
crit_damage.explain: A critical hit deals 1.5 times the damage.

armor_reduction.name: Damage after armor
armor_reduction.explain: Armor cuts damage by its percent, up to a cap of 75 percent (95 with the raised-cap effect). Negative armor adds damage instead.

final_damage.name: Final damage rounding and cap
final_damage.explain: Damage is worked out in decimals, rounded half up once at the end, and capped at 9,999,999 per hit.

normal_hit_chance.name: Normal hit chance (no special hit-rate effects)
normal_hit_chance.expr: to_int(clamp(skill_hit + accu + skill_accu_plus + target_avoid_minus - accu_minus - target_avoid - skill_accu_minus, 5, 95))
normal_hit_chance.explain: Hit chance is the skill's accuracy plus your accuracy minus the target's avoid, and is always kept between 5 and 95 percent. This leaves out special hit-rate effects.

ailment_hit_chance.name: Ailment hit chance (no special effects)
ailment_hit_chance.expr: clamp(skill_hit + effective + target_resist_minus - target_resist + effective_state - target_resist_state, 5, 95)
ailment_hit_chance.explain: Ailment chance is the skill's value plus your effectiveness minus the target's resistance, and is always kept between 5 and 95 percent. This leaves out special effects.

crit_chance.name: Critical hit chance (no special effects)
crit_chance.explain: Critical chance is your crit rate (scaled by the skill's crit setting) minus the target's crit avoidance, and is always kept between 5 and 95 percent. This leaves out special effects.

hit_damage.name: Damage of one hit (core only)
hit_damage.expr: to_int(min(reduced(gained(gained(gained(gained(base, inc_relate_pct), skill_mult_pct), 50 * is_crit), crit_mod_pct * is_crit), to_int(clamp(armor, -2147483647, cap))), 9999999))
hit_damage.explain: Core damage only: base damage, then the skill bonuses, then x1.5 on a crit, then armor, rounded once and capped. It leaves out element conversion, damage-over-time scaling and several other modifiers, so treat it as an estimate.

start_stat_total.name: Starting stat in a run (Lv 1)
start_stat_total.explain: A character's starting value for a stat is the race value plus the job value plus the origin value plus whatever the equipped gear gives.

turn_order.name: Chance the player acts first (percent)
turn_order.explain: Sides alternate. The enemy opens about 1 fight in 3, so the player opens 2 fights in 3.

enemy_tables.name: Enemy stats and skills
needs: Stat and skill tables for each boss

enemy_first_chance.name: Chance the enemy opens the fight (percent)
enemy_first_chance.explain: The enemy opens about 1 fight in 3.

max_hp_final.name: Max HP shown in game
max_hp_final.explain: raw x 0.85 rounded half up, then the extra percent, rounded half up; never below 1.

max_shield_final.name: Max shield shown in game
max_shield_final.explain: raw x 0.85 rounded half up, then the extra percent, rounded half up.

guts_chance.name: Chance Guts keeps an HP stack (percent)
guts_chance.explain: The Guts stat is the percent chance to keep the stack. Its own maximum is not known yet.

drop_chance.name: Drop chance of one drop (percent)
drop_chance.explain: A drop chance of 100 (out of 10,000) drops 1% of the time at the normal rate.

base_damage.name: Base damage of a skill
base_damage.explain: Base damage is the stat times the skill power percent.

parry_chance.name: Parry chance (percent)
parry_chance.explain: The Parry stat is changed by the target's own parry modifiers, then by the attacker's modifiers, rounding after each step. The result is always kept between 0 and 95 percent.

source_armor.name: Damage after source armor
source_armor.explain: Damage over time, delayed, reflect and pursuit damage can be cut by a matching source armor, up to 75 percent (never 95). Negative armor adds damage. It multiplies with normal armor.

hp_stack_gain.name: HP stacks after a gain
hp_stack_gain.explain: A gain adds the effect's value to the stacks and stops at the maximum.

hp_stack_lose.name: HP stacks after a loss
hp_stack_lose.explain: A loss removes the effect's value from the stacks and never goes below 0. A Guts roll can save the stacks first.

hp_stack_reset.name: HP stacks after a reset
hp_stack_reset.explain: A reset sets the stacks to the maximum.
